title: Binding of SARS-CoV-1/2 NSP1 to DNA Polymerase alpha-Primase Inhibits DNA Replication through Reduction of Interaction between DNA and DNA Polymerase alpha-Primase.
authors: Nguyen, Hung Van; Ngoc Lan, Nguyen Le; Li, Mai Suan
journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
one_liner_zh: 该文用MD模拟研究SARS-CoV NSP1与DNA聚合酶α-primase的结合及对DNA复制抑制，属蛋白-DNA互作但非TF-DNA体系，方法为物理模拟，可借鉴其结合自由能与界面分析策略。
abstract: A comprehensive understanding of the atomic level mechanism governing the binding nonstructural protein 1 of SARS-CoV-1 (SARS-CoV-1 NSP1) and SARS-CoV-2 (SARS-CoV-2 NSP1) to Pol alpha-primase is important to advance the development of small molecule inhibitors for the treatment COVID-19. In this study, we use both all-atom steered molecular dynamics (all-atom SMD) and coarse-grained umbrella sampling (coarse-grained US) simulations to assess the binding affinity of SARS-CoV-1 NSP1 and SARS-CoV-2 NSP1 to Pol alpha-primase. Our all-atom SMD and coarse-grained US simulations consistently indicate that SARS-CoV-2 NSP1 exhibits stronger affinity for Pol alpha-primase compared to SARS-CoV-1 NSP1, implying that SARS-CoV-2 poses a greater risk than SARS-CoV-1 in impeding DNA replication for DNA synthesis. Through an energetic decomposition analysis of the interaction energies within these complexes, we identify electrostatic interactions as the primary contributors to the observed difference in binding affinity. We found that hydrogen bonds between Asp33 and Arg616 in SARS1 NSP1-Pol alpha-primase, and Asp33 with Arg616 and Lys655 in SARS2 NSP1-Pol alpha-primase, are critical for the interaction of both SARS-CoV-1 NSP1 and SARS-CoV-2 NSP1 with Pol alpha-primase. Asp33 in SARS-CoV-2 NSP1 shows increased solubility and stability compared to SARS-CoV-1 NSP1, enhancing its association with Pol alpha-primase. This finding lays the groundwork for innovative strategies aimed at inhibiting the interaction between these entities, offering promising avenues for therapeutic intervention against COVID-19. We also estimated the binding free energy of DNA to Pol alpha-primase, SARS1 NSP1-Pol alpha-primase, and SARS2 NSP1-Pol alpha-primase using the MM-PBSA method. The results show the order: Pol alpha-primase-DNA < SARS1 NSP1-Pol alpha-primase-DNA < SARS2 NSP1-Pol alpha-primase-DNA, indicating that both SARS-CoV-1 NSP1 and SARS-CoV-2 NSP1 reduce DNA binding to Pol alpha-primase, suggesting impaired DNA synthesis.
abstract_zh: 全面理解控制SARS-CoV-1非结构蛋白1（SARS-CoV-1 NSP1）和SARS-CoV-2非结构蛋白1（SARS-CoV-2 NSP1）与Pol alpha-primase结合的原子级机制，对于推进治疗COVID-19的小分子抑制剂开发至关重要。在本研究中，我们使用全原子拉伸分子动力学（all-atom SMD）和粗粒化伞形采样（coarse-grained US）模拟来评估SARS-CoV-1 NSP1和SARS-CoV-2 NSP1与Pol alpha-primase的结合亲和力。我们的全原子SMD和粗粒化US模拟一致表明，与SARS-CoV-1 NSP1相比，SARS-CoV-2 NSP1对Pol alpha-primase表现出更强的亲和力，这意味着SARS-CoV-2在阻碍DNA复制以进行DNA合成方面比SARS-CoV-1构成更大的风险。通过对这些复合物内相互作用能量的能量分解分析，我们确定静电相互作用是观察到的结合亲和力差异的主要贡献因素。我们发现，SARS1 NSP1-Pol alpha-primase中Asp33与Arg616之间的氢键，以及SARS2 NSP1-Pol alpha-primase中Asp33与Arg616和Lys655之间的氢键，对SARS-CoV-1 NSP1和SARS-CoV-2 NSP1与Pol alpha-primase的相互作用至关重要。与SARS-CoV-1 NSP1相比，SARS-CoV-2 NSP1中的Asp33表现出更高的溶解性和稳定性，增强了其与Pol alpha-primase的结合。这一发现为旨在抑制这些实体之间相互作用的创新策略奠定了基础，为针对COVID-19的治疗干预提供了有前景的途径。我们还使用MM-PBSA方法估算了DNA与Pol alpha-primase、SARS1 NSP1-Pol alpha-primase和SARS2 NSP1-Pol alpha-primase的结合自由能。结果显示顺序为：Pol alpha-primase-DNA < SARS1 NSP1-Pol alpha-primase-DNA < SARS2 NSP1-Pol alpha-primase-DNA，表明SARS-CoV-1 NSP1和SARS-CoV-2 NSP1均降低了DNA与Pol alpha-primase的结合，提示DNA合成受损。
